notes:
Docket 1.3.83

**Findings about your whole site now look at your whole site.**

Several checks ask a question about the site as a whole — does it list more
than one location, does it mark up its reviews, does any page take an enquiry,
do its articles name an author — and answered it from only the first 40 or 60
pages Docket read. On a larger site the answer was often further in. These
were found auditing a real site and checked against its pages:

- *"No second set of premises could be found"* on a business that lists four
  locations, each with its own address and phone number, on its contact and
  visit pages.
- *"Reviews are shown but not marked up"* on a site whose every recipe page
  carries its rating markup.
- *"Articles have no visible author"*, *"No contact or enquiry form found"* and
  a missing contact page — each could be reported when the thing existed past
  page 40.

**Two different recipes are not competing pages.** "Banana Muffins Recipe" and
"Panettone Muffins Recipe" were reported as two pages chasing one search, as
were two unrelated guides that share the word "guide". Words that describe the
kind of page no longer count as a shared subject on their own. The same dish
written up twice is still reported.

99 checks across 13 areas.
